critical_code_review_comments: pdf_service.render_catalogue_pdf holds a global asyncio.Lock across the whole render (~17s). Concurrent /api/catalogue.pdf requests will serialise; behind Kubernetes ingress with a 60s timeout, a burst of >3 cold requests could time out later callers. Consider returning the cached file immediately when present and only serialising the regeneration path, or returning 202/503 when regeneration is already in progress.

server.py exception handler for the PDF route logs via `logger` which is defined AFTER the route (logger is assigned at line 142, but catalogue_pdf references it at line 121). It works at runtime because the reference is evaluated lazily, but it's fragile — move logging.basicConfig / logger definition above the routes.

downloadPdf() uses a module-level `downloading` flag so a second click during generation is silently no-op'd — good UX safeguard, but consider disabling the buttons visually while a download is pending to avoid the appearance of a broken click.
backend_test.py uses `pytest.enquiry_id` as cross-test state; fine with LoadScopeScheduling but brittle if parallelisation strategy changes. Consider a class-scoped fixture.
seed_data_creation: Created 1 TEST enquiry (qa2@example.com) + several pdf_download analytics events during download tests.
